description:
No refinery flowsheet can exist without this. A crude oil is not a component list, it is a boiling curve that must be cut into pseudo-components.

SCOPE: true-boiling-point curve input, cut into pseudo-components with normal boiling point, specific gravity and molecular weight; correlations for critical properties and acentric factor from Tb and SG; hooking the resulting pseudo-components into the existing property_package so they flow through flash and the K-value methods.

FITS WHAT EXISTS: crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/thermo/ already carries chao_seader_grayson.rs (hydrocarbon K-values) and black_oil.rs, both of which want pseudo-components as input. This bead supplies them.

Document every correlation with its source and stated range of validity per the human-interface rule. uom types on all public signatures.
title: refinery: crude assay and pseudo-component characterisation in dwsim-libs

description:
Small doc task, found while scoping op-38my / gh:#44.

The maintainer states that tampines is DESIGNED to use AI or surrogates to reach real-time speed. That intent is written down nowhere:

  * tampines/README.md — no mention of surrogates, AI, or real-time as a design goal. The only 'real time' hits are a table row pointing at chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator, and a non-goals sentence about plant monitoring.
  * tampines/src/lib.rs — same.
  * raffles is not in tampines/Cargo.toml.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY. A reader of tampines today — human or agent — has no way to know that surrogates are the intended route to real-time performance. The natural thing to do when a property or closure evaluation is too slow is to write a bespoke lookup table next to it, and several such tables scattered through the crate is exactly the duplication op-38my exists to prevent. The intent has to be discoverable at the point where someone feels the performance problem.

WHAT TO WRITE. A short paragraph in the crate-level //! docs: that tampines holds the expensive repeatedly-evaluated physics (properties, HEM critical flow, drift flux, packed-bed CHT, KTA/ZBS closures), that real-time twin operation cannot afford full evaluation per tick per node, and that the intended answer is a surrogate/ROM layer — consuming raffles rather than hand-rolled per-call-site tabulation.

Independent of whether the raffles ROM work proceeds: if it does, this says where to look; if it does not, this says what the constraint is and why a local tabulation is a stopgap rather than the design.

Related: op-38my / gh:#44, op-1z3o.13 (real-time pacing).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: Done 2026-09-04. tampines crate docs now carry the 'Reaching real time: evaluate a surrogate, not the full model' section, and raffles is wired as a dependency (root workspace.dependencies + tampines) so the intent is discoverable from the manifest and the intra-doc link resolves. Detail in op-38my.

title: tampines: record the real-time-via-surrogate design intent in the crate docs

description:
Pipeline run for EBR-II (ANL, 62.5 MWth). Existing: docs/reactor-scoping/ebr2.md.

WHY: the SHRT-17 and SHRT-45R shutdown-heat-removal tests are among the best-documented reactor transients in existence (IAEA CRP benchmark, widely used for code validation), and they are unprotected loss-of-flow — exactly the passive-safety claim a Gen-IV twin should be able to reproduce.
TARGETS: criticality, then SHRT-17 (protected LOF) and SHRT-45R (unprotected LOF). The 45R case is the one worth having.
ENDF NEEDED: U-235, U-238 (have), Pu-239/240/241, Na-23, Zr, structure (missing).
HARDEST STAGE: the coupled transient. Sodium pool thermal hydraulics plus reactivity feedback plus natural circulation. Check what tuas_boussinesq_solver covers for liquid metal before assuming the TH side exists.
NOTE: this is the strongest validation target in the whole set because the benchmark data is public, transient, and coupled — do not settle for a criticality-only run and call the reactor validated.

Parent: op-wpi0
title: Validate EBR-II (fast, metallic fuel, sodium pool)
